target_customer: Real estate listing sites, solar companies, building suppliers and lenders
problem: Home buyers cannot see how much a home will cost in utilities. UtilityScore estimates electricity, gas and water costs and a 1 to 100 score for each home through an API.
business_model: Usage-based data API licensed to real estate and energy companies

founders.name: Brian Gitt
previous_startups: Founded and led several clean energy organizations, including a clean energy consulting firm
founders.background_notes: From the YC page. Education not listed.

competitors.name: Tendril
competitors.what: Energy Score and estimated energy costs for homes, shown on Redfin listings
competitors.traction_then: Covered all homes on Redfin per later coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: Modeling utility costs for 100 million homes needs data assembly from tariffs, home facts and climate, with accuracy issues; standard data engineering with hard modeling parts.

defensibility.rationale: The estimates relied on public home facts and rates. A RESNET analysis found such estimates not robust, and Tendril offered a similar product.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Redfin partnered with Tendril. An RMI update of November 2017 says Tendril and Enerscore were closing their real estate estimate services, so the field shrank.

market_need_then: A July 2015 Inman article described the product as showing which of two identically priced homes costs more to run, targeted at listing sites such as Zillow, Trulia and Redfin. ATTOM Data Solutions added utility costs to its data in 2016.

identity.visual_style: score modeled on Walk Score style 1 to 100 rating
identity.voice_and_tone: plain consumer language about hidden costs

branding.community_and_virality: A score format that real estate sites could embed; partners included Hotpads and ATTOM.

brand_strength.rationale: The descriptive name explained the product and fit the Walk Score pattern, but the brand had limited reach.

pivots.why: reason not stated; the product description is the same

outcome_analysis: UtilityScore sold home utility cost estimates to listing sites and data firms and had partners such as Hotpads and ATTOM. It joined YC S16 with a reported small seed. The YC page lists it as inactive, but no shutdown, acquisition or cause was found, and a 2025 article still mentions its estimates. The cause is not public, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: The seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights, dated 24 Aug 2016, 120K total). The Inman article credits the developer as BKi, an energy consulting and software firm, which may be a related entity; unverified. The Tendril source date of October 2016 is inferred from an image path on Redfin's page, so treat it as approximate and just after the batch. The company website field was empty.
